criteria: Distinguish duplicate enrollment from capacity concurrency

sample-a.atomicity_rollback: One transaction includes enrollment and seat update; explicit rollback on failure.
sample-a.duplicate_vs_capacity: UNIQUE(student,course) prevents same-student duplication; capacity handled separately.
sample-a.overbooking: Conditional update only if seats remain, or suitable isolation.
sample-a.cache: Faster reads; stale data; final authorization uses DB.
sample-a.approach: Conditional seat update or isolation; does not specify an explicit lock.

sample-b.atomicity_rollback: Explicitly groups seat update/enrollment and says rollback if either fails. This topic is present, not missing.
sample-b.duplicate_vs_capacity: False claim UNIQUE prevents two different students taking the final seat.
sample-b.overbooking: No sound capacity-race protection; UNIQUE is incorrectly substituted.
sample-b.cache: Faster reads is recognized, but immediate cache-only approval without DB check is unsafe.
sample-b.approach: Relies on UNIQUE and cached availability, unlike peers with isolation/conditional update/locking.

sample-c.atomicity_rollback: Concurrency transaction/isolation is mentioned, but atomic failure/rollback behavior is explicitly not addressed.
sample-c.duplicate_vs_capacity: Last-seat race diagnosed; repeated same-student registration explicitly not addressed.
sample-c.overbooking: Suitable isolation or lock on course row with recheck.
sample-c.cache: Recognizes stale data risk and refuses cache-only authorization.
sample-c.approach: Explicit row lock and recheck, or isolation; differs from A conditional-update option.

comparison_checks: A vs C: conditional update alternative versus explicit locking/recheck; both mention isolation.
B differs substantively through erroneous UNIQUE/cache-only approach; peers are not automatically correct because they agree.
Do not claim B or A omitted rollback.
C omissions do not make its concurrency/cache analysis wrong.
single_submission: Review A against criteria; comparison_performed=false; comparison says no other submissions are available; no invented peer differences.
privacy: Pass peer texts without IDs/names; output only aggregated topic/approach comparison, no peer identity/language labels/full quotations.
